description:
The corpus's own opinion on a snippet, with a probability per rule.

Difference from `review_code`: there you get the rules and judge yourself,
so two clients can disagree on the same diff. Here the corpus commits: one
question per rule in scope, and the stance decides which threshold applies.

⚠️ NOT a gate, and do not hang it off a CI. Measured over 13 real pairs
(26 measurements, 6 authors, 2018–2026): it lets 38% of violations through,
and a full threshold sweep finds nothing better, because the limit is the
instrument's resolution and not where you cut. What it is good for: ranking
what to look at first and telling you which rule — 11 of 13 right when
comparing a before against an after.

⚠️ Sends the snippet to api.typesafe.ai, a third party. `review_code` never
leaves this server: if the code cannot leave, use that one.

⚠️ REQUIRES A TOKEN on the remote server, because it is the only tool that
costs money and whoever hosts it pays. It goes in the MCP connection's
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Without it this tool says so and
points you at `review_code`, which does the same work for free. This is
stated here on purpose: an MCP client reads this description before
calling, so it is where you find out without having to fail first.

— Opinión del corpus sobre un fragmento, con una probabilidad por regla.
NO es compuerta: deja pasar el 38% de las violaciones, medido sobre 13
pares reales. Manda el fragmento a api.typesafe.ai, un tercero, y PIDE
TOKEN en la cabecera `Authorization: Bearer`. Si el código no puede salir
de la máquina, o no tienes token, usa `review_code`.
